div.l: For he hadde power of confessioıı̄un
And plesaunt was his absolucoıı̄un
And he seid that he was more þan a curet
For of his ordre he was litentiat
He was an esi man to gife penaunce
There as he wist to haue a gode petaunce
For vnto a poer ordre for to geue
Is signe þat a man is wel shryve
For if he gaf he durst make avaunte
That a man were repentaunte
For a man so hard is of his hert
He mai not wepe al þogh he smert
Therefor in stede of wepingꝭes and of praiers
Men most gife siluer vnto þe poer frers
His tipped was ay farsed ful of knyfes
And with pynnes to gife faire wifes
And certein he had a meri note
Wel coude he sing and pley on þe rote
Of thedingꝭes he bare vtterli þe price
His nek was white as floure de lice
Therto he was stronge as a champioıı̄un
He knew wel þe tauerners of þe toun̄
He knew euery Hostiler and eueri tapster
Better than a lazar or a begger
For vnto suche a man as he
Acorded not as be his faculte
To haue with seke lazarus acqueintance
It is not honest it mai not Auaunce
For to dele with such purelers
But al with riche and sullers
And ouer al as profit gan a rise
Curteys he was and lowli of seruice
Ther was no man so vertuous
He was þe best begger in his hous
For þogh a widowe had not a sho
So plesaunte was his Inprincipio
Yit wold he haue a ferthing or he went
His purchase was better þan his rent
And rage he couthe as it were a whelpe
In loue daies coude he moche helpe
For ther he was not like a closterer
With a threde bare cope like a scoler
But he was like a maist̉er or a pope
